_comment: PUBLIC section -> price band map, from the official Sharks 2026-27 full-season seating chart (public marketing material). Band prices are the team's own published per-game averages. Nothing here identifies a seat: it is the whole building's price structure, and no band is marked as ours. See ops#19.
_why: This is the team's own definition of which seats are EQUIVALENT - the baseline comp set for ops#11, replacing a geometric guess. It also lets the app place a seat in the building's price structure with no scraping at all.

_transcriptionStatus.sectionAssignment: NOT TRANSCRIBED - every band's `sections` is empty
_transcriptionStatus._blocker: Section-to-band assignment must be read off the chart's colour coding, and the chart is not in this repo. Guessing it is exactly the failure mode ops#19 warns about, and the same one that made the hand-transcribed tier table need its own validator. Left empty on purpose; scripts/check_price_bands.py reports the gap loudly rather than passing on absent data.
_transcriptionStatus._confidence: The band prices below are TRANSCRIBED, not measured. They are checked for internal consistency by the validator, not against an external source.

_priceNote: avgPerGame is the published full-season average per game. `renew` is the renewal rate, `new` the new-buyer rate. Some bands publish only one of the two; absent means not published, not zero.
_rowScopeNote: Most bands are section-level: a section belongs to exactly one band. Promenade Row 1 is NOT - it is row 1 *inside* promenade sections, priced separately from the rows behind it. So the map is really (section, rowScope) -> band, and the coverage check groups by rowScope. Missing this makes 'every section assigned exactly once' unsatisfiable and would push someone toward deleting the check instead of fixing the model.
_ringsNote: Section labels in CLOCKWISE order around each seating level, starting from centre ice on the Sharks-bench side. Transcribed from Ticketmaster's public static seatmap for SAP Center (mapsapi.tmol.io/.../staticImage), NOT from the Sharks pricing chart - so this is arena geometry and carries no price information. CONFIDENCE: read off a PNG by eye, so corroborated rather than trusted: scripts/check_price_bands.py asserts the lower ring's six missing numbers (105/108/111/119/122/125) sit in mirror-symmetric positions about the 101-115 axis, which a misread would almost certainly break. This is what makes the arc-contiguity and mirror-symmetry placement checks runnable once section->band assignment exists.
_familyNote: `family` groups bands that form one published price ladder, and `rank` 1 is the most expensive. The lower / promenade / upper / club ladders are named as such on the chart. The 'premium' family (Glass, Teal, Orange) is NOT - those are product names, and grouping them into a ranked ladder is an INFERENCE from their prices. It buys a real ordering check; if the chart shows they are unrelated products, split them into separate families rather than weakening the check.
_ringsOpenQuestion: The band names in this file (Promenade 1-3, Promenade Row 1, Upper Attack 1-2, Upper Goal 1-2, Club 1-5, Glass, Teal, Orange) do NOT map onto the 100/200/PL section numbering visible on Ticketmaster's map. Ticketmaster shows two rings plus nine PL sections; the Sharks' chart implies at least four priced levels. So the level names cannot be matched to rings by inference - that mapping has to come from the Sharks' own colour-coded chart. Do not guess it. See ops#19.
